headline: Nusrat murder: HC upholds death penalty for 2, acquits 10
summary: The High Court has confirmed the death sentences of former principal SM Siraj-Ud-Dowlah and aide Shahadat Hossain Shamim, while commuting four others to life imprisonment.
details: The High Court has confirmed the death sentences of former principal of Sonagazi Islamia Fazil Madrasa, SM Siraj-Ud-Dowlah, and his close aide Shahadat Hossain Shamim in the murder case of student Nusrat Jahan Rafi.
The court also commuted the death sentences of four other convicts to life imprisonment and acquitted 10 others from the case.
In a significant move, the HC ordered the law ministry to curtail the judicial power of Feni court judge Mamunur Rashid for handing down death sentences to the accused in a wholesale manner.
The verdict was pronounced after 17 working days of hearings on the death reference and appeals filed by the convicts challenging the trial court's original verdict.
Nusrat, a 19-year-old student, was allegedly sexually harassed by the madrasa principal, SM Siraj-Ud-Dowlah, in March 2019.
Following the report, Siraj's accomplices allegedly took Nusrat to the madrasa roof and set her on fire on April 6, 2019. She died from her injuries on April 10.
Previously, the Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal in Feni had handed down death sentences to all 16 accused in October 2019.
caption:
Two men face the gallows after the High Court upheld their death sentences for the brutal murder of madrasa student Nusrat Jahan Rafi.

The High Court has confirmed the death sentences of former principal of Sonagazi Islamia Fazil Madrasa, SM Siraj-Ud-Dowlah, and his close aide Shahadat Hossain Shamim in the murder case of student Nusrat Jahan Rafi.

The court also commuted the death sentences of four other convicts to life imprisonment and acquitted 10 others from the case.

In a significant move, the HC ordered the law ministry to curtail the judicial power of Feni court judge Mamunur Rashid for handing down death sentences to the accused in a wholesale manner.

The verdict was pronounced after 17 working days of hearings on the death reference and appeals filed by the convicts challenging the trial court's original verdict.

Nusrat, a 19-year-old student, was allegedly sexually harassed by the madrasa principal, SM Siraj-Ud-Dowlah, in March 2019.

Following the report, Siraj's accomplices allegedly took Nusrat to the madrasa roof and set her on fire on April 6, 2019. She died from her injuries on April 10.

Previously, the Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal in Feni had handed down death sentences to all 16 accused in October 2019.

headline_marked: ICT [[sends three journalists to jail]] in crimes against humanity case
headline: ICT sends three journalists to jail in crimes against humanity case
summary: Shyamal Dutta, Mozammel Babu, and Farzana Rupa were ordered to be jailed following allegations of provocative remarks during the July Uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has ordered three journalists to be sent to jail in connection with a crimes against humanity case linked to the July Uprising.

The accused include Shyamal Dutta, editor of Bhorer Kagoj and former Jatiya Press Club general secretary, Mozammel Babu, managing director and editor-in-chief of Ekattor TV, and Farzana Rupa, a principal correspondent for the same channel.
Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim alleged that the three made provocative remarks during a press conference at Gono Bhaban on July 14, 2024.
The prosecution claims these remarks prompted then-prime minister Sheikh Hasina to refer to protesters as ‘Razakars’ and ‘children of Razakars’, which sparked widespread protests.
It is further alleged that the previously peaceful quota reform movement turned violent after attacks on students by Chhatra League and Jubo League activists.
The defense counsel for Shyamal Dutta urged the tribunal to consider that there were no elements of crimes against humanity against his client before ordering the arrest.
caption:
Three journalists sent to jail by the ICT for 'provocative remarks' during the July Uprising.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has ordered three journalists to be sent to jail in connection with a crimes against humanity case linked to the July Uprising.

The accused include Shyamal Dutta, editor of Bhorer Kagoj and former Jatiya Press Club general secretary, Mozammel Babu, managing director and editor-in-chief of Ekattor TV, and Farzana Rupa, a principal correspondent for the same channel.

Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim alleged that the three made provocative remarks during a press conference at Gono Bhaban on July 14, 2024.

The prosecution claims these remarks prompted then-prime minister Sheikh Hasina to refer to protesters as ‘Razakars’ and ‘children of Razakars’, which sparked widespread protests.

It is further alleged that the previously peaceful quota reform movement turned violent after attacks on students by Chhatra League and Jubo League activists.

The defense counsel for Shyamal Dutta urged the tribunal to consider that there were no elements of crimes against humanity against his client before ordering the arrest.
